chunks: Shurayḥ replied: Yes, Amīr al-mu’minīn, it is so. Amīr al-mu’minīn cast an angry look at him and said to him:

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin, Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali
key_terms.شُرَيْحٌ: Shurayh, the renowned judge of Kufa appointed by Imam Ali
key_terms.نَظَرَ مُغْضَبٍ: An angry look, indicating displeasure or a corrective gesture

ai.seo_question: What was the context of Imam Ali's angry look towards Judge Shurayh?
ai.summary: This brief exchange highlights the dynamic between Imam Ali (AS) and his chief judge, Shurayh ibn al-Harith, illustrating the Imam's rigorous standards for judicial decorum and authority. The angry glance serves as a non-verbal correction, emphasizing that while Shurayh was a capable jurist, he was expected to maintain the dignity and responsiveness befitting the Amir al-Mu'minin's court. This moment underscores the Shia scholarly view of the Imam as both a legislator and a meticulous supervisor of justice.
